in_greek.name: Λίσση
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Λίσση προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'Λίζα', που σημαίνει 'Απόλυτη αγάπη'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα συνδέεται με την αγάπη και την πίστη στον Θεό. Η χρήση του ονόματος Λίσση ήταν συνηθισμένη στην αρχαία Ελλάδα και αργότερα υιοθετήθηκε από την Εκκλησία ως μέρος της παράδοσης της.

in_latin.name: Lissy
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lissy derivatur a verbo Latino 'lis', quod significat 'Deus meus iudicium'. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen hoc adhibebatur ad significandum iudicium Dei super populum. Culturae christianae occidentalis nomen Lissy receperunt et in traditione christiana permanebat.

in_english.long_meaning: The name Lissy originates from Hebrew and Greek roots, meaning 'God is my judge' or 'beloved'. It has biblical connections through its etymology from 'Elis' or 'Liza', signifying divine judgment or absolute love. Historically, Lissy has been used across Jewish and Christian traditions, symbolizing faith, devotion, and spiritual guidance. The name carries connotations of righteousness, piety, and a strong connection to divine providence.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lissy gained recognition in the English-speaking world when it was adopted by the David family in the Bible (2 Samuel 11:17). The Saxon and Norman influence on the English language contributed to the spelling and pronunciation of the name as Lissy. It has been popular in various parts of Europe, including Ireland, Scotland, and England, particularly during the Middle Ages. The name also has a connection to the Greek legend of Leander and Hero, who would meet at the Temple of Aphrodite on a rocky promontory in Abydos called Heroon Lea, also known as Lissa.

It is also a name that can inspire confidence and trust in God, as it conveys a sense of reliability and steadfastness. Ultimately, Lissy encourages those who bear this name to reflect on God's faithfulness and to trust in His promises.
